newsitem.title: UK: Kvaerner has no plans to sell Heavylift.
newsitem.headline: Kvaerner has no plans to sell Heavylift.

text.p: Heavylift Cargo Airlines earns about 25 percent profit on turnover and this is why overall parent company Kvaerner ASA has no plans to sell the carrier, said Heavylift managing director Michael Hayles.

He acknowledged that, as a "non-core activity", the subject of Heavylift's sale to a management buy-out team had been raised when Kvaerner purchased Heavylift's direct parent, Trafalgar House, last year.
"But the UK finance earned by Heavylift, which Kvaerner needs, makes such a buy-out, or a sale, unlikely," he told an air cargo conference here.

He declined to answer whether or not Heavylift is about to acquire two Airbus freighters to add to its own fleet of Belfast, Ilyushin IL-76, AN-12 and Hercules freighters and Antonov 124-100s operated in partnership with Russia's Volga-Dnepr.
"It (the Airbus freighter) has its limitations and this would make it a specialist-type operation, he said.
